# Sirach Chapter 4 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 4

---

1 My child, do not deprive the poor of their living, and do not keep the needy waiting with empty eyes.

2 Do not add to the grief of the hungry, nor provoke a person who is already in distress.

3 Do not make a troubled heart more bitter, nor delay giving to one who is in need.

4 Do not reject the appeal of the afflicted, and do not turn your face away from the poor.

5 Do not avert your eyes from the needy, and give no one reason to curse you.

6 For if someone curses you out of bitterness, his Maker will hear his prayer.

7 Gain the goodwill of the assembly, and before a person of influence, show deference.

8 Lend your ear to the poor, and answer them gently and humbly.

9 Rescue the wronged from the hand of the wrongdoer, and do not be cowardly in rendering judgment.

10 Be like a father to orphans, and like a husband to their mother; then you will be like a child of the Most High, and he will love you more than a mother loves her child.

11 Wisdom nurtures her children and gives help to those who seek her.

12 Whoever loves her loves life, and those who seek her from early on will be filled with joy.

13 Whoever holds fast to her obtains glory, and the Lord blesses the house she enters.

14 Those who serve her serve the Holy One; the Lord loves those who love her.

15 Whoever obeys her will render judgment among the nations, and whoever heeds her will live in security.

16 If he trusts her, he will inherit her; his descendants will hold her as their possession.

17 At first she will lead him along winding paths, bringing fear and timidity upon him, and tormenting him with her discipline until she fully trusts him, testing him with her ordinances.

18 Then she will come back to him on the straight path and gladden him, and will reveal her secrets to him.

19 But if he goes astray, she will abandon him and hand him over to his ruin.

20 Watch for the opportune moment and guard yourself from evil; do not be ashamed of your whole self.

21 For there is a shame that leads to sin, and there is a shame that leads to glory and favor.

22 Do not favor anyone to your own harm, nor show partiality to anyone at your own expense.

23 Do not hesitate to speak at the right moment, and do not conceal your wisdom.

24 For wisdom is recognized through speech, and instruction through the words of the tongue.

25 Do not contradict the truth, and be ashamed of your ignorance.

26 Do not be ashamed to confess your sins, and do not try to stop a river in flood.

27 Do not defer to a foolish person, and do not show partiality to a person of influence.

28 Fight to the death for truth, and the Lord God will fight for you.

29 Do not be reckless with your words, nor slack in your deeds.

30 Do not be like a lion in your own home, and do not be suspicious of your household.

31 Do not let your hand be open to receive and closed when it is time to give.

---

## Council Notes

**On v.10 "son/child of the Most High":** Greek huios Hypsistou. Ben Sira is not making a Christological claim; he uses the phrase to describe the one who embodies divine compassion. SOPHIA uses "child" (gender-neutral) to reflect that the promise extends to all who act thus.

**On vv.17-19 — Wisdom's testing:** This is the most sophisticated passage in chs.1-10. Ben Sira depicts Wisdom as a disciplining teacher who first terrifies, then trusts. PNEUMA captures this drama particularly well. SOPHIA follows EMET's structure but incorporates LOGOS's clarity.

**On v.26 "stop a river":** LOGOS has "stop a river with your hand"; EMET has "against the current of a river." Greek kata rhous potamou = "against the current of a river." Proverbial: don't resist the unstoppable. SOPHIA: "stop a river in flood."

**On v.31 "hand open/closed":** Memorable antithesis. All agents captured it. SOPHIA preserves the chiasm: open to receive / closed to give.
